messages:
ben: heads-up — after the 'stitch' kernel selection rollout to canary, host-side CPU for tokenization jumped ~22% on p50 traffic. profiler flame shows parse -> tokenize -> smallwrite hot path. logs pasted below. anyone seen similar?

ben: ```
host_parse_ns=1.2ms tok_ns=0.9ms smallwrites=372 evict_thr=0.02
kernel_choice=stitch_v3 seq_len_dist=8..64 batch_hint=auto
```

alice: :eyes: saw traces earlier but assumed kv-evict noise. 22% is large. what's the traffic mix on that canary? small chatty reqs?

ben: mostly short chat messages (avg seq ~28 tokens). throughput steady, but CPU per-request up. KV cache hit rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.74 after rollout.

kevin: that drop lines up with the sampler change that biases against small-writes to prefer big batch kernels. stitch_v3 picks kernels for amortized throughput; maybe it prefers a kernel that forces extra prefix merging on host.

carmen: quick hypothesis: kernel picks that optimize GPU amortization are increasing host-side framing/parse cost for lots of small requests. batching heuristics need to account for host tokenize cost, not just GPU cycles.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary rollout stitch_v3 completed at 2025-05-12T14:22:01Z on cluster-r53 :rocket:

aj: can we get a callstack snippet from the profiler? we need to confirm whether tokenize syscall or grpc framing is the dominant CPU consumer.

ben: attached snippet (abbreviated):
```
1000ms total
  420ms parse::parse_frame
  380ms tokenizer::tokenize_inline
   80ms http2::writev_small
   60ms kvcache::evict_sample
```

kevin: tokenize_inline being that high is suspicious — we didn't change tokenizer recently. stitch_v3 must be changing request shapes or forcing extra copies. maybe we're coalescing frames differently causing double-parse.

alice: quick mitigation options: revert kernel selection on canary; or patch sampler to avoid switching kernels for seq_len < 64; or change preparse to peel tokenization into the hot path (inline) to avoid extra copy.

carmen: agree. short-term revert buy us time. medium-term we should update kernel selection scoring to include host_tokenize_cost estimate. current score = alpha*gpu_ms + beta*mem but beta ignores CPU parse cost.

ben: I ran a microbench: when stitch_v3 forces 'windowed_coalesce' kernel, host parse increases by ~30% vs legacy. smallwrites up 3x. kernel traces show an extra framing pass.

kevin: concrete plan: 1) revert stitch_v3 on canary now (quick). 2) add a telemetry field for host_parse_estimate in kernel profiler. 3) change sampler rule: prefer legacy kernel when seq_len<=48 and p50_latency_target<50ms.

aj: +1 to plan. i'll trigger rollback if you want. we should also add an ephemeral flag to disable frame-coalesce on ingress for canary to test.

ben: please rollback. also opening a perf PR with the profiler trace and sample corpus. will include a small harness to repro with avg seq 28.

alice: i'll start the bisect tomorrow and try swapping only the batching heuristic part of stitch_v3 to isolate kernel-choice vs framing-change.

kevin: i'll prototype quick change to sampler: add host_cpu_penalty term using recent parse telemetry; fallback to legacy if penalty > 0.15.

carmen: note for follow-up: KV cache behavior changed too — eviction rate up. likely because framing change increases ephemeral keys (prefix variants). add an eviction dedupe and increase shard warmup window.

ben: task list: alice=bisect, kevin=sampler patch, aj=rollback (in progress), carmen=kv warmup tweak, ben=perf repro + traces.

aj: rollback kicked off. canary should flip in ~90s. will post once done. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-notify: rollback stitch_v3 completed at 2025-05-12T14:24:12Z on cluster-r53 — traffic now on legacy kernels.

ben: post-rollback quick check: host CPU p50 back to baseline, KV hit recovers to 0.86. good call.

kevin: thanks — still going to add the host_cost term to kernel scoring so next rollout doesn't regress host-side.

alice: logging action items in https://redwood-internal/boards/ENG-RUNTIME-Perf (will link PRs there).

carmen: let's add a unit test that simulates small-chatty seq distribution and asserts kernel selection won't pick coalesce-heavy kernels.

ben: agreed. closing thread once PRs land. thx all.
